summary: A genuinely connected, honest audio phase built on a thin, schematic surface. The shared graph is real and correct — one AudioContext, per-layer Piano A/B buses, an ordered Mod1→Mod2→Delay→Amp/EQ→Comp→Reverb chain, To-Rotary send, master gain and limiter, one destination — with real dry/wet crossfades, per-unit and all-effects bypass, delay feedback+filter, and panel controls actually wired into the engine via presentationToAudioState/updateState. Real-boundary offline-render tests prove instrument distinction, velocity, layers, master level, SUSTPED, fallback, reverb wet, and combined bypass. The decisive limitation for this phase is honesty-correct but requirement-missing: Grand/Upright/Electric are OfflineAudioContext-synthesized tone sets, truthfully declared as 'synthesized' (sampleSources: []), not the bundled recorded sample sets the phase requires — so instrumentBreadth is capped low though it is NOT the 0 reserved for generated buffers presented as recordings. Secondary gaps: within-unit effect types are largely undifferentiated (Mod1's six types collapse to one tremolo; Amp's seven types are drive-scaled; LP24/HP24 not real filters), no tests exercise Mod1/Mod2/Delay/Amp/Comp individually or per-type distinction, both layers always share one effect-state object (resolveEffectsForLayer returns the same fx in every branch), and the surface is a wireframe far from the reference photo with a narrow layout that collapses to unusable overlap.

evidence: stage2-desktop.png is near-identical to stage1-desktop.png (only the Piano type LED and Program OLED text changed: 'Grand Model' vs 'Init Program'), so Phase 1 surface is retained without regression at 1440x900.

Absolute fidelity vs reference/nord-stage-4-73.jpg is low: sections are plain HTML sliders and text-labeled rectangles, not the Nord's knobs, rocker switches, LED ladders, drawbars, and dense legends; six ordered sections and the 73-key keybed are present but schematic.
stage2-narrow.png (390x844) collapses the deck into overlapping, truncated boxes that are effectively unusable for inspection, though the red chassis and full keybed survive.

control-bindings.ts maps panel IDs to audio state (piano-type-led-*, piano-layer-a/b-*, fx-*-bypass, fx-*-type/rate/amount/mix, fx-all-bypass, perf-master-level) and instrument.ts routes functional controls through presentationToAudioState→engine.updateState.
Type selection updates the Program OLED text ('<Type> Model') and the active type LED, giving coherent visual feedback for the selected piano type.

Focus/target and per-layer effect state are only weakly represented: resolveEffectsForLayer returns the same fx object in every branch, so A/B effect state is shared, and the schematic panel exposes little distinct per-unit on/target display beyond generic sliders.

samples.ts synthesizes all six sets via OfflineAudioContext (renderTone/buildSet) and stamps provenance: 'synthesized'; IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json lists them under generatedSources with sampleSources: [] and states Grand/Upright/Electric are 'audibly distinct synthesized sample sets — not recordings' — honest, but NOT the bundled recorded sample sets the phase requires.

This is honesty-correct (not the score-0 case of generated buffers presented as recordings), but the required recorded/redistributable-file provenance for Grand/Upright/Electric is absent, so the requirement is substantially unmet.

Distinction is shallow: 5 root notes (C2–C6) x 2 velocity layers per type, differing only by harmonic-ratio/decay/brightness profiles; the engine.test.ts 'six piano types distinct' test passes via signalsDiffer but this reflects synthesized profile differences, not sampled instruments.

engine.ts noteOn iterates layers A and B, applies per-layer octave shift and level, and tracks per-layer voice ownership; getActiveVoiceCountForLayer confirms it in the 'both layers independent ownership' test (A=1, B=1, total 2).
Layer enable/level are real: 'respects layer enable and level' renders onlyA vs both and asserts rms(both) > rms(onlyA); layerInputs gain ramps to 0 when a layer is disabled or section is off.

Cleanup is sound (releaseVoice cancels/ramps gain and stops sources; blur/allNotesOff clear voices), but octave is derived from a single knob mapping and both layers share type selection (piano-type-led sets A and B together), a modest depth gap.

velocityToGain implements KB Touch (Heavy/Medium/Light) and Dyn Comp (Off/1/2/3) curves; the 'KB Touch and Dyn Comp change output' test renders and asserts signalsDiffer, and 'master level scales output' asserts rms(high) > rms(low).

Unison (pan spread + detune), String Res (added sub-oscillator), and Soft Release (longer release except Clav) are wired in spawnVoice/applyUnison and affect the graph, so several controls are canonically audible.

Timbre is crude (timbreRate returns small playbackRate nudges from a 4-entry map, not a per-type-family timbre) and only KB Touch/Dyn Comp/master have dedicated rendered assertions — Unison, String Res, Soft Release, and Timbre are not individually verified by rendered-audio tests.

engine.test.ts exercises pointer, computer-key (with repeat suppression), and MIDI note/velocity/CC64 sustain through the real engine, plus denied/disconnected MIDI ignored; instrument.ts wires all three plus blur cleanup.
Sustain honors per-layer SUSTPED: 'honors SUSTPED per layer' asserts layer A holds and layer B releases after setSustain(true)+noteOff; polyphony limit 32 with deterministic oldest-voice stealing.

Fallback is truthful: forceSampleFail yields status 'fallback' (never 'ready'), fallback triangle buffer still plays (noteOn > 0); soft/sostenuto beyond simple sustain is not claimed, and the engine AudioContext is not closed on component unmount (only lifecycle.dispose), a minor cleanup gap.

engine.ts builds one context: layerInputs A/B → LayerEffectChain → layerLevel → mixBus → masterGain → limiter (DynamicsCompressor threshold -3, ratio 20) → single context.destination; the shared Rotary also feeds mixBus.
Gain staging uses short setTargetAtTime ramps (RAMP=0.012–0.015) on master, layer inputs, layer level, and every wet/dry to avoid clicks; masterGain scales with Master Level (value/127*0.7).

Cleanup: dispose() stops LFOs, disconnects chains/rotary/masterGain and closes the context; renderOffline/measureOutputLevel prove the whole path renders non-silent audio offline, but the live component never calls engine.dispose() on unmount.

All seven units are real, connected nodes (not labels): Mod1 LFO→wet-gain AM, Mod2 short modulated delay+feedback, Delay (delay+filtered feedback), Amp WaveShaper drive + 3-band EQ, Compressor (DynamicsCompressor), Reverb ConvolverNode, shared Rotary LFO tremolo — so disconnected-node/label score-0 does not apply.

Only reverb has a dedicated rendered assertion ('reverb wet changes rendered signal', signalsDiffer + rms>0) plus a combined mod1+delay vs all-bypass difference test; Mod1, Mod2, Delay, Amp/EQ, and Compressor are not individually proven to process audio by tests.

Within-unit type distinction is largely unimplemented: Mod1's six spec types collapse to one sine tremolo (only type===2 boosts depth), Amp's seven types only scale drive by type*0.15 (LP24/HP24 not real filters, To Rotary handled separately), and no test proves any per-type audible difference the spec's 'every listed type audibly distinct' requires.

Signal order matches the spec (Mod1→Mod2→Delay→Amp/EQ→Comp→Reverb, Reverb before Rotary), per-unit dry/wet and bypass are real crossfades, all-effects bypass routes input→bypassGain around the chain, and Delay has a genuine filtered feedback loop (delayNode→filter→feedback→delayNode).

To Rotary is wired: 'to rotary routes layer into shared rotary' asserts getEffectChain('A').isToRotary()===true and the chain zeroes its own layerLevel and opens toRotarySend into the shared Rotary input.

Routing depth is limited: resolveEffectsForLayer returns the same fx object in every branch so both layers always share one effect-state (no truly independent per-layer params), group/global-mode flags exist in state but do not change which state each chain receives, and focus-follows-layer, group, and global routing have no rendered-audio tests.

Functional controls immediately update audio via setControlValue/interactControl→syncEngineFromPresentation→engine.updateState, and the status bar shows 'Piano: ready · Voices: N' reflecting active voice count.
Type selection produces coherent LED + OLED text feedback ('<Type> Model'); master level, layer level/enable, and effect wet/bypass changes are audible via the shared graph.

Visual feedback is thin because the surface is schematic — most effect/perf controls are generic sliders/boxes without distinct LED, meter, or value displays, so 'coherent display + LED + sound' feedback is partial.

Denied/disconnected MIDI is ignored (tested), forced sample failure enters a labeled playable fallback without reporting 'ready' (tested), and forceError yields status 'error' with noteOn returning -1.

Focus loss is handled (window blur → blurCleanup stops all owned voices; sustain reset), and a 32-voice cap with deterministic oldest-voice stealing plus a master limiter guards against runaway polyphony/clipping.
Rapid effect-parameter changes ramp smoothly via setTargetAtTime, but there is no explicit test for rapid effect-change stress or sustained layered-polyphony clipping recovery.

Clean boundaries: samples.ts (SampleLibrary), effects-chain.ts (LayerEffectChain + SharedRotary), engine.ts (voice/layer/bus/master), boundaries.ts injectable AudioContextFactory/TimingBoundary, and state/control-bindings.ts separating presentation from audio state.
Injectable platform APIs make tests deterministic offline (OfflineAudioContext factory, mock MIDI port, timing boundary) with no network/device dependency.

Extensibility for Phase 3 is reasonable (per-layer chains, shared Rotary, resolvable effect state), though resolveEffectsForLayer is a no-op stub and per-layer independent effect params are not yet modeled, which will need rework for Organ/Synth chains.

Tests cross the real Web Audio boundary via renderOffline/OfflineAudioContext.startRendering() and signal-analysis helpers (rms, earlyRms, signalsDiffer) rather than mocks — instrument distinction, velocity direction, layer level, master level, SUSTPED, fallback, reverb wet, and bypass difference are all asserted on rendered signals.
Voice/cleanup behavior is asserted on the real engine (active voice counts to 0 after release/all-notes-off/blur; per-layer ownership counts).

Coverage gaps weaken it: no rendered test isolates Mod1/Mod2/Delay/Amp/Comp, no per-type-distinction test, and no routing test for focus/group/global or delay-feedback audibility — several required effects.processing/effects.routing behaviors rely on inspection, not measurement.

Code is compact and consistently named with low duplication; feature-matrix.json retains all Phase 1 IDs and adds every Phase 2 ID mapped to real, non-empty test files, and Phase 1 lifecycle/inputs/status tests remain present (regression.phase1).
Voice cleanup cancels scheduled values, ramps gain, and stops sources with guarded try/catch; ramps avoid clicks and the limiter protects the master path.

Maintainability caveats: resolveEffectsForLayer is dead branching, timbreRate/effect-type mappings are ad hoc magic-number tables, and the live component leaks the AudioContext on unmount (no engine.dispose), so render/audio stability under long sessions is not fully guaranteed.

issues.detail: Phase-2 hard requirement unmet (but declared honestly): Grand/Upright/Electric are OfflineAudioContext-synthesized tone sets, not bundled recorded sample sets. samples.ts stamps provenance 'synthesized' and IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json sets sampleSources: [] and calls them 'not recordings' — so this is not the score-0 case of generated buffers presented as recordings, but the required recorded/redistributable-file provenance is absent, capping instrumentBreadth.

Within-unit effect-type distinction is largely unimplemented: Mod1's six spec types collapse to one sine tremolo (only Ring Mod boosts depth), Amp/EQ's seven types are drive-scaled with LP24/HP24 not realized as filters, and no rendered test proves per-type audible difference, so the spec's 'every listed effect type audibly distinct' is not satisfied.

resolveEffectsForLayer returns the same fx object in every branch, so Piano A and B always share one effect-state; group/global-mode flags exist but do not change per-chain state, and there are no rendered tests for focus/group/global routing.

The surface is a schematic wireframe far from reference/nord-stage-4-73.jpg (plain sliders/labeled boxes rather than knobs/rockers/LED ladders/drawbars), and the 390x844 narrow layout collapses the deck into overlapping, truncated controls.
The live component never calls engine.dispose() on unmount (only lifecycle.dispose), so the AudioContext is not closed — a resource-cleanup gap not covered by tests.
